content.text: Jeevan Umang is a **participating, non-linked, whole-life plan** that offers a dual benefit of both income and protection to your family. In simple terms, you pay premiums for a limited period, and in return, you get a guaranteed annual survival benefit from the end of the premium paying term until you reach age 100. It also provides a lump sum payment on maturity (at age 100) or on death. It's one of LIC's flagship products for long-term, guaranteed retirement income.

sections.title: How the Calculator Works: Formulas & Assumptions

content.heading: Premium Calculation
content.body:
The calculator estimates your premium based on several factors:

  • Base Premium: This is determined by LIC's official rate tables based on your age, the sum assured, and the premium paying term (PPT). Younger ages and longer PPTs result in lower annual premiums.
  • Modal Loading: Paying monthly, quarterly, or half-yearly is slightly more expensive than paying annually. Our tool applies these standard 'modal loadings' (e.g., multiplying the annual premium by ~0.0879 for monthly).
  • Rider Premiums: If you select optional riders like Accidental Death Benefit, their specific premium is added.
  • GST: GST is applied at ~4.5% for the first year and ~2.25% for subsequent years on the base and rider premiums.

content.heading: Benefit Calculation
content.body:
• Survival Benefit: This is the core promise of Jeevan Umang. It is a guaranteed 8% of the Basic Sum Assured, paid annually after the PPT ends, until age 100 or death, whichever is earlier.
  • Bonuses: As a participating plan, it accrues Simple Reversionary Bonuses and may also receive a Final Additional Bonus (FAB). These are not guaranteed and depend on LIC's profits. Our calculator uses illustrative rates for projection.
  • Death Benefit: The amount paid to your nominee is the Sum Assured on Death plus accrued bonuses. This is guaranteed to be at least 105% of all premiums paid.

content.heading: Case Study 1: The Young Professional (Age 30)
content.body:

content.heading: Case Study 3: Planning for a Child (Age 1 as Life Assured)
content.body:
Goal: Create a financial safety net and future income for a child.
Inputs: Child's Age 1, Parent's Age 30, BSA ₹5 Lakh, PPT 25 years.
Annual Premium: ≈ ₹17,000 (+GST).
The Result: From the child's age of 27, they start receiving ₹40,000 annually. It can act as a supplementary income early in their career. The policy also serves as a substantial asset they can take a loan against for a home or business later in life.

content.text: Jeevan Umang offers excellent liquidity options after the policy has been in force for some time.

items: Loan Facility: You can take a loan against the policy once it has acquired a surrender value (typically after paying premiums for 2 full years). The loan amount can be up to 90% of the surrender value for in-force policies. This is a great way to access funds in an emergency without terminating your cover.

Surrender Value: If you must exit the policy, you can surrender it after 2 full years of premium payment. You will receive the higher of the Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV) or the Special Surrender Value (SSV).

Paid-Up Policy: A smarter alternative to surrendering. If you stop paying premiums after 2 years, your policy becomes 'paid-up' with a proportionally reduced Sum Assured. You will still be eligible for a reduced survival income and death benefit without paying any more premiums.

content.heading: Loan Calculation Example
content.body: Suppose after 10 years, your policy for a ₹10 Lakh BSA has a Special Surrender Value (SSV) of ₹4 Lakh. You could take a loan of up to 90% of this amount, which is ₹3.6 Lakh, to meet an urgent financial need. The loan and its interest would be adjusted against future payouts or the final claim amount.

sections.title: Jeevan Umang Calculator: Frequently Asked Questions

items.q: What is the survival benefit in Jeevan Umang?
items.a: It is a guaranteed annual payment equal to 8% of your Basic Sum Assured. This payment starts after your premium paying term ends and continues every year until you reach age 100 or until death, whichever is earlier.

items.q: Is the income from Jeevan Umang taxable?
items.a: As per current tax laws, the survival benefits and maturity/death benefits received from LIC policies are generally tax-free under Section 10(10D), subject to certain conditions. It's always best to consult a tax advisor for the latest rules.

items.q: What happens if I stop paying the premium?
items.a: If you have paid premiums for at least two full years, your policy will not lapse but will become a 'paid-up' policy. You will receive reduced benefits (death cover, survival income, and maturity value) in proportion to the number of premiums you have paid.

items.q: Can I take a loan on my Jeevan Umang policy?
items.a: Yes, a loan facility is available after the policy has acquired a surrender value (typically after 2 years of premium payment). This provides a good liquidity option in case of emergencies.

items.q: What is the difference between Jeevan Umang and Jeevan Utsav?
items.a: Jeevan Umang provides a fixed 8% of the Sum Assured as annual income. Jeevan Utsav provides a higher 10% of the Sum Assured but offers a 'Flexi' option to accumulate this income at a guaranteed 5.5% interest rate instead of taking it annually. Jeevan Utsav also has a shorter maximum premium paying term (16 years vs 30 for Umang).

sections.title: Final Verdict: Who Should Consider Jeevan Umang?

content.text: LIC's Jeevan Umang is a powerful tool for individuals seeking a disciplined, long-term savings plan that provides a guaranteed, tax-free income stream during retirement. It is particularly suitable for those who prioritize safety and predictability over aggressive, market-linked growth. If your goal is to create a reliable 'pension' for yourself that is immune to market volatility, Jeevan Umang is one of the most compelling options available in the Indian insurance market. Use this calculator to see how it can fit into your financial future.
